pseudonym

SOO-duh-nim -- from Greek pseudes ('false') + onyma ('name'). · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Pseudonym is a fake name used to conceal someone's real identity.

During the underground chess tournament, the mysterious top-ranked player competed only under a pseudonym, refusing to reveal even his home country.

Worked Example

Long before revealing his real identity, the masked street artist signed every mural with the same mysterious pseudonym.

Notice a pseudonym is specifically a name -- not a disguise, not a costume, not a made-up backstory -- just an assumed false name standing in for someone's real one.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

alias: An alias is any assumed name used to hide who you are, and the word often carries a whiff of the police report — criminals travel under aliases. Pseudonym is the neutral, bookish term for the same trick and is the usual word for authors and artists shielding their identity.

nom de plume: A nom de plume is strictly a writer's invented name — the term means 'pen name' and applies to no one but authors. Pseudonym is the wider umbrella: any false name concealing a real identity, whether the hider is a journalist, a painter, or a spy.

stage name: A stage name is the polished name a performer works under — chosen for sparkle, and usually no secret at all, since fans may know the real one. A pseudonym exists to conceal: its whole job is keeping the real identity hidden. One is branding; the other is cover.

code name: A code name is a label an organization assigns for internal secrecy — Operation Nightfall, or an agent called 'Condor' by headquarters. Nobody signs public work with a code name. A pseudonym is a personal false name its owner uses openly in public, precisely so strangers never learn the real one.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

legal name: a person's official, real name

birth name: the name someone was given at birth, as opposed to any assumed name

Build the Word

The pieces

root — pseudo-

root — pseudo-: false, fake (Greek (pseudes))

root — -onym

root — -onym: name (Greek (onyma))

Put it together

Put it together: Pseudonym combines the Greek roots for 'false' and 'name' -- quite literally, a 'false name.' Both roots are extremely common in English, showing up in everything from pseudoscience to synonym.

Use the root in a new word: pseudoscience

Use the root in a new word: pseudoscience: Astrology is often criticized as pseudoscience because its claims are not supported by testable evidence.

Root Check

Word Choice

Pseudonym refers specifically to a false name. A general disguise or cover story might involve a fake appearance or backstory too -- a pseudonym is just the name part of a hidden identity.
